items.title: Ray Drummond interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003
items.q: I’m going to be the next Rockefeller

ctx.x: No, no. None of that. No, no. There are two issues with this convention. I’m not sure — first of all you have to understand I’m a political sociologist. That’s my degree. That’s what my undergraduate degree was really in. And so I see two specific missions that aren’t necessarily compatible that are not exclusive and they don’t conflict with one another but they have parts of each other that do conflict. Okay on the one hand this convention and this organization is about jazz education okay? But on the other hand…

convention has now taken on an additional responsibility, especially now since the Jazz Times convention folded or actually more accurately has folded a small portion of itself into this particular convention. So you’ve got really a pull between the commercial forces of the media, of the entertainment industry, meaning the record companies and other media companies that are interested in the commercial media. You’ve got them pulling at the educational because they’re trying to get them to feed them and yet there…

time in 25 years I’m back now in an institutional setting as a faculty member and I’m really enjoying it again. But then I knew I would because I like teaching. But I took myself off the market for 25 years because I wanted to be fully a professional musician. I didn’t want — it wasn’t that it was a problem being an educator it’s just that I wanted to see what it was going to be like for me to be out there earning my own living without an institution behind me, without any of the — I mean it’s not a safety net,…
